questions.question: Why should a cultural dance be studied in its social and historical context?
choices: Context helps explain the dance's meanings, roles, and changes over time
It reveals one universal meaning for every dancer
It removes the need to observe movement
It proves that all members of a culture dance alike

questions.question: Hula is associated with which Indigenous culture?
choices: Inuit culture
Native Hawaiian culture
Māori culture
Sámi culture

questions.question: Bharatanatyam is a classical dance tradition associated with
choices: Peru
Norway
India
Mexico

questions.question: What is one respectful practice when learning a dance from a culture different from one's own?
choices: Treat the dance as a costume or joke
Claim the dance has no cultural meaning
Assume one video represents every community
Use reliable sources and acknowledge the tradition and its practitioners

questions.question: Why is it important to distinguish a community's traditional practice from a commercial performance inspired by it?
choices: The purpose, context, and cultural authority may differ
Commercial work is always more authentic
Traditional practices never change
The movement vocabulary must be unrelated

questions.question: A class studies a dance connected to a harvest celebration. Which question is useful?
choices: What is the dancers' exact height?
How does the dance relate to the community's seasonal or ceremonial context?
Which costume is most expensive?
Can the dance be removed from its community?

questions.question: What can music, costume, and movement together communicate in a cultural dance?
choices: A single meaning that applies to all cultures
Only the choreographer's age
Shared histories, identities, values, or occasions, depending on the tradition
A universal language with no context

questions.question: Why should a student avoid saying that one dance represents an entire continent?
choices: Continents have no dance
All dances come from one country
Movement cannot be compared
Regions and communities contain many distinct traditions

questions.question: A dance is passed through generations but changes over time. What does this show?
choices: Traditions can be preserved and adapted by communities
Traditions must stay identical
The dance has lost all cultural value
Change prevents historical study

questions.question: When presenting a cultural dance, what information should be credited when available?
choices: Only the costume designer
The tradition, community or practitioners, and source of the learning material
No sources are needed
A made-up origin story

questions.question: Why might a dance be performed in a circle?
choices: Every circle dance has the same origin
The shape proves the dance is ancient
The formation may support shared participation or a particular social meaning
Circles prevent audience viewing

questions.question: A dance includes gestures that carry culturally specific meaning. What should a learner do?
choices: Assign a meaning from personal preference
Remove every gesture
Assume gestures mean the same thing everywhere
Learn the meaning from knowledgeable sources rather than guessing

questions.question: Which statement about cultural dance is most accurate?
choices: Dance can be artistic, social, ceremonial, communal, or some combination
Every cultural dance is a stage performance
All traditions are religious
Cultural dances have no audiences

questions.question: Why is consent and community input important when documenting a cultural dance?
choices: It makes the recording more colorful
It respects participants and can shape what should be recorded or shared
It proves every movement is public property
It replaces historical research

questions.question: What is a useful way to compare dances from two cultures?
choices: Say they are the same because both use rhythm
Rank them by difficulty
Compare specific movement and performance features while preserving their distinct contexts
Ignore who performs them

questions.question: A dance is performed during a community procession. What can its setting contribute?
choices: It proves the dance has no choreographer
It makes the dance a theater piece only
It determines the tempo
It may connect movement with place, public participation, and occasion

questions.question: What should a student do if sources disagree about a dance's origin?
choices: Report the uncertainty and compare the sources' evidence and perspectives
Choose the most dramatic story
Invent a single answer
Ignore all sources

questions.question: Why might a cultural dance include repeated steps or patterns?
choices: It proves the dance is simple
Repetition can support participation, structure, or symbolic meaning
It removes the role of music
It guarantees all dancers perform identically

questions.question: A dance is taught in a school assembly. What should the teacher consider?
choices: Whether the dance can be shortened without context
Whether students can imitate costumes
Whether the context and teaching approach represent the tradition respectfully
Whether the tradition is currently popular

questions.question: What is the strongest way to describe a cultural dance?
choices: Use broad stereotypes
Rely on a single costume image
Assume personal interpretation is fact
Name observable features and explain them using reliable cultural context
